item.text: {"confident":true,"explanation":"The curves intersect at x=±2, so D={(x,y): −2≤x≤2, x²−6≤y≤2−x²}. Statement I is true because its rectangle contains all of D and f is zero outside D. Statement II is false: its rectangle includes positive-area regions outside D where x²+y² is positive, and it does not contain D (indeed, f as defined is not defined on all of D). Statement III is false because its rectangle omits a positive-area portion of D below y=−2, where the integrand is positive.
